subject: Assessment playbook: exit gates and acceptance tests for the evaluation
messages:
From: Sanjay Reddy <sanjay.reddy@aureliatx.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: Priya Shah <pshah@aureliatx.com>
Date: Wed, 08 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Evaluation kickoff + what success looks like (Aurelia)

Tessa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We have internal approval to run a formal evaluation of Redwood for inference on our internal document classification workload. Before we kick off, our evaluation committee asked for a short MAP that spells out success criteria, clear exit gates, and a concise set of acceptance tests so stakeholders can sign off quickly.

Attached is a short evaluation_scope.pdf with dataset size and the primary use cases (batch extraction + low-latency API for clinical note ingestion). High level asks from our side:
- 99th percentile inference latency < 250ms for the short-path API (typical request size ~512 tokens)
- Token cost target: < $0.0009/token average across runs
- Functional accuracy: entity extraction F1 >= 0.88 on our labeled sample
- Security: SOC2 evidence + KMS integration checklist

Can you provide a one‑page MAP and a checklist of acceptance tests we can circulate? Also include the minimal set of test inputs we should run and the owner for each gate.

Best,
Sanjay Reddy
Head of AIOps, Aurelia Therapeutics

Attachment: evaluation_scope.pdf (PDF, 148KB)

From: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
To: Sanjay Reddy <sanjay.reddy@aureliatx.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <pshah@aureliatx.com>, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evaluation kickoff + what success looks like (Aurelia)

Hi Sanjay / Priya —

Thanks — attached is a first draft MAP and acceptance test matrix (redwood_map_draft.xlsx). High-level summary below; the workbook has line items and owners.

Summary (TL;DR):
- Duration: 4 weeks of active testing (2-week baseline, 2-week optimization + validation)
- Primary exit gates: latency SLO, cost per token target, extraction F1, and security/compliance checklist
- Acceptance tests: functional (F1 on labeled set), perf (p95/p99 and cold-start), and regression (round-trip prompt fidelity)
- Owners: Aurelia owns labeled test set + business signoff; Redwood provides test harness, automation scripts, and infra; Marcus will run the perf sweeps and quantization profiles.

Next steps:
1) Priya to confirm labeled dataset delivery date.
2) Sign-off on the MAP spreadsheet (I put a proposed sign-off matrix in tab "Signoff").
3) Kick off tech onboarding call next Monday (we can provision a dedicated pool for the run).

I pulled the acceptance thresholds from your note but left them editable in the sheet — please flag any changes.

—Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Director, Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_map_draft.xlsx (Excel, 64KB)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: acceptance thresholds and concrete test scenarios

Tessa, Marcus —

Quick internal update on the draft MAP after reviewing the labeled sample stats:
- Move 99th percentile latency target to 300ms for the first baseline run (512 tokens) to avoid failing on network variability; keep 250ms as the optimized target for the final gate.
- Add a cold-cache latency test (first request after cache invalidation) and a warm-cache p99. Include KV cache hit-rate >= 85% as an explanatory metric.
- Cost: report both raw token unit cost and blended cost including batching overhead. Add a guardrail: if blended cost > 1.15x target, we fail the cost gate.
- Functional: require F1 >= 0.88 on the primary labeled set AND no more than a 2-point drop on the secondary blind set.

Proposed new exit gates (mapped to sign-off owners in the spreadsheet):
A. Security/compliance evidence + KMS complete — Security (Aurelia) — must be satisfied before any data is loaded.
B. Baseline perf run completed and p95/p99 meet the baseline thresholds — Redwood infra (Marcus) + Aurelia engineering to validate.
C. Optimization run (quantization/batching) shows cost target met and F1 maintained — Product/SE (Tessa & Marcus) + Aurelia PO.
D. Final business sign-off (Aurelia stakeholder) — legal/ops review completed.

I'll add these as an \"Exit gates\" tab and enumerate the measurement scripts. Marcus, can you prepare the perf harness and schedule the perf sweep this week?

-Karthik
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: Sanjay Reddy <sanjay.reddy@aureliatx.com>, Priya Shah <pshah@aureliatx.com>, tessa_morgan@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: MAP + acceptance playbook (finalized items for signoff)

Sanjay / Priya —

Per our internal alignment, below is the playbook we propose to include in the MAP. I pasted the key items here so your execs have a compact view to circulate. The attached spreadsheet contains the scripts, pass/fail thresholds, and timelines.

Playbook highlights (actionable items):
1) Timeline: Week 0 (onboarding, security checks) -> Week 1 (baseline perf & functional tests) -> Week 2 (optimization: quantization & batching) -> Week 3 (validation & regression) -> Week 4 (final signoff).
2) Exit gate details (must be green to progress):
   - Gate 1: Security & Data Access — Evidence: SOC2 report + KMS test vector run (owner: Aurelia Security).
   - Gate 2: Baseline Perf — Metrics: p95 <= 180ms, p99 <= 300ms (baseline), cold-start <= 1.1s. Measurement: 10k sample run, 95% CI reported (owner: Redwood infra).
   - Gate 3: Cost Optimization — Metric: blended token cost <= $0.0009/token OR within 1.15x with documented optimization plan. Measurement: aggregated billable tokens across runs (owner: Redwood finance ops).
   - Gate 4: Functional Quality — Metric: primary F1 >= 0.88 AND secondary blind set drop <= 2 pts. Measurement: labeled test harness (owner: Aurelia ML).
   - Gate 5: Business Acceptance — Signed signoff form and SOW executed.
3) Acceptance test matrix (examples):
   - FT-01: Entity extraction accuracy on labeled set (script: run_entity_eval.py) -> PASS if F1 >= 0.88.
   - PT-02: Latency sweep (script: perf_sweep_v2.sh) -> PASS if p99 <= 300ms on baseline, optimized target p99 <= 250ms.
   - RT-03: Regression check (script: regen_prompt_check.py) -> PASS if no more than 1% deviation in top-1 intent mapping.

Action items for this week:
- Priya: confirm dataset drop date (we need CSV + labels).
- Aurelia Sec: provide SOC2 evidence by Friday.
- Redwood: we will provision a dedicated pool and run baseline perf on Thursday 16th.

If these items look good I will convert the spreadsheet to a sign-off PDF and share a one-page MAP summary for your execs.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Related link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-map-playbook
Attachment note: perf scripts live in the Drive folder.

Subject: Re: MAP + acceptance playbook (finalized items for signoff)

Marcus / Tessa —

This is exactly what we need. Quick notes and we're good to sign:
- Accept the relaxed baseline p99 of 300ms for Week 1 as long as the optimized target 250ms is a locked gate for Week 3.
- We will deliver the labeled dataset (primary + secondary blind) by Wednesday 7/21.
- Security team confirms SOC2 evidence and KMS test vector by Friday 7/24.

Please include an explicit rollback plan in the MAP (if quality drops >3 pts during optimization run we revert to the baseline model and we call a triage meeting). Also add a short clause that Redwood will provide the automation scripts and a CSV of all raw runs for audit.

Once you add those two small items, I'll circulate for business sign-off and attach the SOW.

Thanks — Sanjay
Head of AIOps, Aurelia Therapeutics
